title: Functions, Structs, Methods, and Interfaces
summary: Design focused functions and domain models using multiple returns, pointers, methods, constructors, embedding, and small interfaces.

Test the contract with build and runtime evidence

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Functions can return multiple values, commonly a result and error. Go passes arguments by value; a pointer allows deliberate mutation of the pointed object but does not convey ownership. Structs group fields, and methods attach behavior to a named type. Keep fields unexported when updates must preserve invariants, and provide a constructor that validates initial state. Interfaces are satisfied implicitly by method sets. Define small interfaces at the consumer boundary and accept concrete types until substitution is actually useful. A nil interface and an interface containing a typed nil pointer are different.
